| President Trump spent his first hours in the White House taking an axe to the horrible executive orders issued during Joe Biden’s miserable time in office. Breitbart has compiled a helpful list, which includes:
* Biden’s order to make “equity,” rather than “equality,” the focus of federal policy;
* Biden’s order to include illegal aliens in the Census;
* Biden’s order to impose coronavirus mandates and restrictions;
* Biden’s order to allow transgender individuals to serve in the military;
* Biden’s order to ban private prisons;
* Biden’s order to prioritize climate change; to ease immigration enforcement;
* Biden’s order to revoke sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC);
* Biden’s order to establish a court-packing commission to make the Supreme Court permanently liberal;
* Biden’s order to prioritize diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in federal hiring;
* Biden’s order to restrict offshore oil and gas development;
* Biden’s order to impose sanctions on Israelis linked to the political right;
* Biden’s order to rescind Cuba’s designation as a state sponsor of terrorism; and
* Biden’s order to revoke many of Trump’s executive orders from his first term.

Looking at this list, it’s hard to fathom just how ridiculous some of the Biden executive actions were. President Trump’s decision to swiftly end them is common sense, but it predictably caused outrage on the left. President Trump is taking action to restore American energy dominance by ending the Biden administration’s war on the fossil fuel industry. He’s ending ridiculous “DEI” programs within the federal government, focusing rightly on merit instead. And he’s preserving critical institutions in America like the Supreme Court by stopping in its tracks efforts to pack the court. These Day One actions from President Trump outline a simple but consequential agenda for the next four years: focus on the basics of what the American government is supposed to do, and end all the superfluous BS of the last four years.

It turns out, Americans largely agree with President Trump’s position on abortion. President Trump nominated justices to our Supreme Court who overturned the disastrous Roe v. Wade and returned the debate over abortion back to our political process. President Trump’s resounding victory proved that Americans have a far more conservative view on abortion than the left would like to believe.

It is up to the Pro Life movement - in Congress, among activists, all of us - to make sure Americans know exactly where both parties stand on this critical issue. The March for Life on Washington in the first week of President Trump’s return to the White House is symbolic of the fact that we are winning hearts and minds on this issue.

Hi Friend,
With Donald Trump’s second term now underway, I’m reaching out for a few reasons. I know that emotions are running high across the country - I’m certainly experiencing that myself and here in Philadelphia.
I want you to know that I have been and will continue to roll up my sleeves and work to ensure that Philadelphia residents are safe and protected from the many new threats we face. We cannot afford to become overwhelmed by the volume of news or tune out what is happening. We are in this together and I am taking every action seriously with a laser-focus on safeguarding Philadelphia.
For example, last year, as the Public Health Committee Chair, I passed a resolution focusing on vaccine education and recognizing the critical importance of vaccines for children . In addition to the good work for Philadelphia that I’ve had planned, I intend to keep a close eye on our new administration to ensure that data-driven health policy is supported for all of our residents.
With an eye on ensuring that Philadelphians are safe and supported, I am watching the policy changes of the Trump administration closely. From immigration to energy and from LGBT protections to reproductive rights, I am prepared for the inevitable fights to come. Fight back, we will.
I also want to hear from you. Please respond to this email and let me know your current concerns, hopes, and ideas. It is essential that we stay connected and share vital community resources in these times and I look forward to hearing from you.
As always, I am endlessly optimistic for Philadelphia and deeply grateful for your continued support. I carry you with me each and every day.
Nina

Peter, earlier this month, I was officially sworn in to serve America once again - this time in the United States Senate.

On Monday, I watched as President Donald J. Trump took the Oath of Office to become our 47th President.

It's been a historic month for hardworking Americans. Under our new GOP leadership, we will rein in spending, restore accountability, and bring common sense back to Washington, D.C..

* Cutting government fat and reining in wasteful spending

* Unleashing American energy to lower costs for all Americans
* Protecting the men and women who serve in our Armed Forces to make sure nothing like the disastrous Afghanistan withdrawal never happens again
* Or something else

body:
| | Peter,

I firmly believe that in Southwest Washington, and most places in the U.S., that we have more in common than divides us. Since day one of my time in Congress, I have upheld this belief by putting place over politics, and working across the aisle to get things done.

I attended the Presidential Inauguration on behalf of WA-03 to witness democracy at work, and reaffirm my willingness to work with anyone on the issues that matter most to you.

But, I was struck by something at the ceremony, Peter: Billionaire tech CEOs (one of whom spent nearly a million dollars to defeat me last year) seated in front of Cabinet members. I don’t know about you, Peter, but to me, the world’s richest men taking seats that otherwise would have gone to public servants doesn’t align with the core principles of our democracy.

When the wealthiest individuals wield this kind of influence, are they shaping policies that benefit working Americans—or policies that serve their own interests? This is cronyism in action and it will not bring down prices at the grocery store, make our communities safer, or level the playing field for small businesses.

I didn’t buy my seat in Congress, Peter – we built a people-powered movement that fought for our shared values. That’s how democracy should work.

[But, our fight isn’t over. I’m still counting on your grassroots support as we prepare for the challenges ahead. Since I was eight years old, I've been fascinated by natural disasters.
If you've followed me for any length of time, you know I'm a survivor of multiple tornadoes and some of the worst hurricanes on record (Hurricanes Georges (1998), Katrina (2005), etc).
I've lived through disasters in Mississippi, Louisiana, Florida and even New York (Snowmageddon of 2011).
After my experience during Hurricane Katrina (I was 16 at the time), I developed a low-key, side-plot mission to join the administrative wing of FEMA someday.
I was working my way toward that quickly when I was hired and then 10 months later promoted in my job at DOH working with Florida's Department of Emergency Management.
I've seen how local, state and federal agencies work together during a disaster. I've seen states fail (Hurricanes Katrina, Michael, and Ian) and triumph (Hurricane Dorian).
Few disasters today are limited to just one state, and the same disaster may not affect two states in the same way. Examples: Mississippi vs New Orleans after Katrina, and Florida vs the Carolinas in Helene.
That's why cooperation and planning across all local and state authorities with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has become such a critical part of avoiding disaster during disaster.
Today, **Trump announced his plan to eliminate FEMA.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/923feec6-7fb4-450b-9e91-b62b4d058d4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In 2024, the United States experienced 27 billion-dollar weather and climate related disasters (excluding all other disaster types). Perhaps that's why Trump is targeting FEMA -- they work to protect and save people from the climate crisis Trump wants to ignore.
FEMA was created in 1979 by President Jimmy Carter.
The goal was to streamline the federal government's efforts to respond to and manage disasters.
Before FEMA's creation, disaster response and recovery efforts were handled by several different agencies, which sometimes led to inefficiency.
By consolidating these efforts under FEMA, the U.S. government aimed to improve coordination and provide a more effective response during national emergencies. Since its creation, FEMA has played a central role in disaster management, from providing immediate relief to helping with long-term recovery efforts.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3991291c-8f5e-4547-afe3-3b7a9035eaea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Since that time, FEMA has responded to more than 10,000 emergencies and disasters.
In just the last year, FEMA has worked 185 declared disasters and emergencies occurring at just the county level.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f5924c70-817d-47c6-9905-a94824f87fb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
All county-level declared disasters FEMA worked from 1/1/2024-1/1/2025, via https://www.fema.gov/data-visualization/disaster-declarations-states-and-counties
FEMA not only provides immediate aid, but it also helps in disaster preparedness. It runs training programs and distributes grants to state and local governments to improve their ability to respond quickly.
During the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, FEMA coordinated the distribution of personal protective equipment (PPE) and ventilators to hospitals, ensuring that critical resources were available where they were needed most.
If FEMA didn't exist, there would be no inter-state management to ensure resources were properly allocated.
FEMA also supports long-term recovery efforts, helping communities rebuild infrastructure, housing, and businesses.
The agency also works with the National Weather Service to provide timely alerts for storms and other potential hazards, reducing the risk of injury and loss of life. Ultimately, FEMA's role in disaster response ensures that the nation is better prepared and more resilient when catastrophe strikes.
There is certainly a lot that could be improved -- more transparent operations (especially at the state level), improved data sharing (especially at the federal level), and ending political appointments to administration (see: Jared Moskowitz' failures during COVID).
No government agency is without its flaws - whether local, state or federal. That doesn't mean you eliminate the nation's most critical disaster resource as disasters are becoming more frequent and intense.
FEMA also works with homeland security to address threats of domestic terrorism.
Perhaps that's what this is all about.

| Peter,

One of my favorite things about campaigning for Governor of Virginia is traveling across the Commonwealth, listening directly to Virginians about their challenges and aspirations, and celebrating the beauty of Virginia. This past weekend, I had the opportunity to meet with hundreds of voters across 10 communities in Southwest Virginia and Southside Virginia.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/100924853/524370716/1993432096?refcode=BLU_EM_ASFG_2025-01-24_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzhhNDRjYWEtOWNkYS1lZjExLTg4ZjgtMDAyMjQ4MmE5NTc5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CkNZYrxPg01VnC0QCmMpY6FfRRXofGKBQztinMGNUK8=)

body:
I’m committed to the same values I’ve always been.
#
Derek, I’ve seen the rumors on social media that I’m going to switch parties, and I wanted you to hear the truth directly from me.
**It’s not gonna happen.**
I’ll work across the aisle to get things done for PA, but I’m committed to the same values I’ve always been:

➡️ the GOP needs to leave LGBTQ+ people alone

Many affected by Hurricane Helene complained that their communities received little-no help from government relief agencies like FEMA. name: Kerry McQuisten (Newsletter)
subject: Our D.C. Celebration!
body:
| | | | |
# From on the Ground in DC!
---
| |
---
| Somewhere in the back of my mind was once the little-kid whisper, "If I were President, I would do _this _..." But as an adult, I literally just watched President Trump, signature by signature, enact as if going down through my own checklist all the things I've wanted for America. I can't even describe the emotion, but I'm sure most of you reading this already know what I mean.
For a week and a half, Solomon and I were in Washington D.C. We went to start the process of fundraising for the [Oregon Conservative Caucus](https://sptr.eocampaign1.com/f/a/LL_S6u_6mjBSnWmwygxEig~~/AAAHUQA~/RgRpdpnoP0UgMzE2YWJmN2IyMDQyNTAxZWY2ODZmZGY4MmZmZjA4OWFEKWh0dHBzOi8vd3d3Lm9yZWdvbmNvbnNlcnZhdGl2ZWNhdWN1cy5jb20vVwVzcGNldUIKZ5ToFJRnDwwLfFIUZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb21YBAAAX2M~). We were also there to attend a reception with [Republicans Overseas (RO)](https://sptr.eocampaign1.com/f/a/mPoD3_ItjRhzm8tNvezuMw~~/AAAHUQA~/RgRpdpnoP0UgMzM0ZDQzNjVmZjNmNDAyMzU2YjE0MmVkNDQ5Y2RmMjdEIGh0dHBzOi8vcmVwdWJsaWNhbnNvdmVyc2Vhcy5jb20vVwVzcGNldUIKZ5ToFJRnDwwLfFIUZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb21YBAAAX2M~) and conduct whatever RO business we could while some of us were at least in the same city! We did the usual touristy stuff, but the primary reason for being in DC was to attend the inaugural events, bring to a close one political chapter, and enter the next. We started this chapter a few yards in front of President Trump at Mar-a-Lago when he announced his candidacy and were there for most of the major events along the way. The inauguration was the magnificent cherry on top of it all.
This inaugural committee did things differently from committees of the past. Swearing-in invitations weren't given to convention delegates. Ticket types that were transferrable before weren't this time, which meant we couldn't provide invitations as we would have liked. The members of the RNC weren't invited to most events, and were only given standing tickets to the swearing-in - a first. While this was appropriate for the "Food and Flowers" RNC members, this wasn't right at all for the members who worked their posteriors off for this election. The focus was very much on fundraising, and toward that end, there was record-breaking success. The inauguration and its trappings are paid for through those donations. However, the overselling of major-donor events created security issues with mobbed receptions with relatively unprotected cabinet nominees and donors. I was front and center with Solomon for one such event, and it was the only time I was aware we were at risk and felt the need to be hypervigilant. I saw the clear concern in the eyes of the cabinet members and security, and I heard the comments. Bonus: I did get to meet Ace Frehley from KISS and Kevin O'Leary there!
But the rest? It was great! I started getting _really _excited when we went to the Decatur Carriage House to pick up our gift bag full of goodies. Commemorative everything - including two bottles of the special Diet Coke with the President Trump inaugural label!
We popped in and out of RNC events as their meeting was held prior to the other festivities. (New RNC Co-Chair: K.C. Crosbie! Yes!!!) I can't emphasize enough how blessed we are to not be tied down by the Oregon Republican Party with Solomon's former National Committeeman seat. That may sound shocking, but we would've never been able to accomplish anything we've accomplished this year for President Trump if we'd been stuck spinning our wheels in a decaying, drama-filled organization. Republicans Overseas' GOTV efforts doubled the overseas vote for Trump in Israel alone. (Numbers in other countries still pending.) We brought in over $50 million dollars in earned media for Trump's ending-double-taxation policy pledge. We'll see this policy through the legislative process and help up to nine million overseas Americans. The Trump campaign authorized $1.25 million for our efforts at the time, and we didn't use a dime! Separate from that, Solomon and I raised amounts solidly up in the six figures for the T47C and then the Inaugural Committee, and in doing so, met some new friends from Idaho and Tennessee. What an epic year!
At the RNC's Victory Reception I was able to tell Ambassador Callista Gingrich how we'd watched her husband (Newt) choke up during the convention during the moment President Trump accepted his nomination. They were seated in a suite about 10' from us in Milwaukee and I'll never forget it. We ran into CPAC organizer Matt Schlapp who Solomon has known for years, so I got to meet his wife Mercedes, former White House Communications Director, for the first time. The best part was getting to catch up with RO/RNC friends before we headed across town to the Crypto Ball thanks to a private invitation from the new Crypto Czar David Sacks. Now THAT was a party. The first person we ran into was former French presidential candidate Eric Zemmour on the red carpet. Speaker Mike Johnson hung out with us for a little bit, and for those who call him a weak RINO, he honestly isn't. I'm solidly conservative and like him more every time we talk with him - and I understand better the position he's in and why President Trump trusts him. We scooted out of there when Snoop Dogg came on stage - not really our cup of tea and it was already late.
I don't know if there was a security threat that inspired the decision to move the swearing-in ceremony from outdoors to under the Capitol Rotunda. Security threats happen all the time to presidents. But I do know that it truly was bitter cold outside and most of the audience couldn't have withstood 10 hours in that weather. Million-dollar-donors, Trump/Vance family members, some international dignitaries, the Justices, incoming cabinet members, and some members of Congress were about all who could fit inside the rotunda. Other dignitaries, elected officials, spouses, and the governors of states were seated off-camera in a nearby room. Standing ticketholders were informed that they could try for seats in the Capitol One Arena by getting into line hours early. So that was a bit of a cattle call. That left those of us with seated swearing-in tickets up in the air until the night before the ceremony. We originally were placed in the "lime" seated area up front, but as there was no more room with the governors, ended up in private suites in the arena. Even that was questioned when we arrived at the arena with our police motorcycle escort and were told by security that we were supposed to have taken the other bus to the rotunda. (It was taking two hours to get from arena to rotunda.) Everyone was confused but it worked out.
In the end, we took up the third level of the arena with a dozen or so people per suite. We were with Eric Trump's friends "since before he even dated Lara!" they told us. We were warm, comfortable, and had our own restroom, food and drinks. I'll tell you, I lost it when President Trump recited his oath, and I'm really not a crier. Then I looked at Solomon and around our suite, and there wasn't a dry eye. A lady from West Palm blessedly had a stash of Kleenex. The only drawback with the arena setting is that what was a dignified ceremony a few blocks away became more of a rally setting there.
Events often overlapped, so we left early during the parade. We always had a half-mile walk or longer to get outside the perimeter to find an Uber. We rested and changed into our black-tie attire for the Starlight Ball, which is the headliner ball where President Trump made his final appearance on inauguration day. Javier Milei, the President of Argentina, was there with his translator, bodyguard and his sister, and remembered who we were from prior communication. I was so proud of not botching my Spanish with him! All my languages are rusty at present.
While the Liberty Ball had over 13,000, I guessed maybe 1,000 were at the Starlight. Attendees either paid $50,000 to attend and hoped to be approved with a big donor package, or were invited. We did a little lobbying for that ending-double-taxation legislation as members of the House and Senate were milling around. Celebs like Mike Tyson, Jillian Michaels, and Vince Vaughn were in the crowd. I taught Solomon my rock concert skills for holding the rail so that we were only feet away from President Trump and the First Lady, Vice President Vance and the Second Lady, and the Trump family for their dance on the stage. When Fox News lost their feed, Solomon and I each took unobstructed video of the entire thing. You can find mine on my [Facebook page](https://sptr.eocampaign1.com/f/a/FnKujHnod-TqcyKsNLIonw~~/AAAHUQA~/RgRpdpnoP0UgN2EzNzEzNTU0NmI0OTQ5MmQxNGM5ZGU2NzMzZjJhODVEMGh0dHBzOi8vd3d3LmZhY2Vib29rLmNvbS9LZXJyeU1jUXVpc3RlbmZvck9yZWdvblcFc3BjZXVCCmeU6BSUZw8MC3xSFGRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tWAQAAF9j), though I had to lower the resolution there to get it to upload.
Last, we heard about some fraud going on with the grifter events dotted outside the recognized celebrations. Promises of celebrities who never had any intention of appearing as part of the VIP packages that were sold using their names. High ticket prices for no adequate food or drink. Promises of a possible Trump appearance that was NEVER ever going to happen. Fines for various violations in the middle of the event. Demands for refunds only to find there would be none... Some of the donors to these cons had literally given enough money that if they'd called me or Solomon, we could have had them at least at unsanctioned balls where they really would have had a genuine inaugural experience. But on the polar opposite of that, we closed our trip with a conversation with the family of an incoming cabinet secretary who reminded us that there are people who really are trying to do right by us, will uphold Trump's agenda, and honestly - are just people who deserve a little grace.
We're back home in Oregon now. And it's time to bring this energy shift here ... All I can say is this: [**OREGON CONSERVATIVE CAUCUS**](https://sptr.eocampaign1.com/f/a/LL_S6u_6mjBSnWmwygxEig~~/AAAHUQA~/RgRpdpnoP0UgMzE2YWJmN2IyMDQyNTAxZWY2ODZmZGY4MmZmZjA4OWFEKWh0dHBzOi8vd3d3Lm9yZWdvbmNvbnNlcnZhdGl2ZWNhdWN1cy5jb20vVwVzcGNldUIKZ5ToFJRnDwwLfFIUZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb21YBAAAX2M~), baby!
---

**Oregon Conservative Caucus Update**
---
| **Help us flip Oregon red! **Since my last newsletter, we received notice from the IRS that we're officially designated as a 501(c)(4)! We need members and donations. We're creating something amazing for our state here...
**Link: **[**Oregon Conservative Caucus | Nonprofit**](https://sptr.eocampaign1.com/f/a/LL_S6u_6mjBSnWmwygxEig~~/AAAHUQA~/RgRpdpnoP0UgMzE2YWJmN2IyMDQyNTAxZWY2ODZmZGY4MmZmZjA4OWFEKWh0dHBzOi8vd3d3Lm9yZWdvbmNvbnNlcnZhdGl2ZWNhdWN1cy5jb20vVwVzcGNldUIKZ5ToFJRnDwwLfFIUZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb21YBAAAX2M~)

We ran into CPAC organizer Matt Schlapp who Solomon has known for years, so I got to meet his wife Mercedes, former White House Communications Director, for the first time. The best part was getting to catch up with RO/RNC friends before we headed across town to the Crypto Ball thanks to a private invitation from the new Crypto Czar David Sacks. Now THAT was a party. The first person we ran into was former French presidential candidate Eric Zemmour on the red carpet. Speaker Mike Johnson hung out with us for a little bit, and for those who call him a weak RINO, he honestly isn't. I'm solidly conservative and like him more every time we talk with him - and I understand better the position he's in and why President Trump trusts him. We scooted out of there when Snoop Dogg came on stage - not really our cup of tea and it was already late. I don't know if there was a security threat that inspired the decision to move the swearing-in ceremony from outdoors to under the Capitol Rotunda. Security threats happen all the time to presidents. But I do know that it truly was bitter cold outside and most of the audience couldn't have withstood 10 hours in that weather. Million-dollar-donors, Trump/Vance family members, some international dignitaries, the Justices, incoming cabinet members, and some members of Congress were about all who could fit inside the rotunda. Other dignitaries, elected officials, spouses, and the governors of states were seated off-camera in a nearby room. Standing ticketholders were informed that they could try for seats in the Capitol One Arena by getting into line hours early. So that was a bit of a cattle call. That left those of us with seated swearing-in tickets up in the air until the night before the ceremony. We originally were placed in the "lime" seated area up front, but as there was no more room with the governors, ended up in private suites in the arena. Even that was questioned when we arrived at the arena with our police motorcycle escort and were told by security that we were supposed to have taken the other bus to the rotunda. (It was taking two hours to get from arena to rotunda.) Everyone was confused but it worked out. In the end, we took up the third level of the arena with a dozen or so people per suite. We were with Eric Trump's friends "since before he even dated Lara!" they told us. We were warm, comfortable, and had our own restroom, food and drinks. I'll tell you, I lost it when President Trump recited his oath, and I'm really not a crier. Then I looked at Solomon and around our suite, and there wasn't a dry eye. A lady from West Palm blessedly had a stash of Kleenex. The only drawback with the arena setting is that what was a dignified ceremony a few blocks away became more of a rally setting there. Events often overlapped, so we left early during the parade. We always had a half-mile walk or longer to get outside the perimeter to find an Uber. We rested and changed into our black-tie attire for the Starlight Ball, which is the headliner ball where President Trump made his final appearance on inauguration day. Javier Milei, the President of Argentina, was there with his translator, bodyguard and his sister, and remembered who we were from prior communication. I was so proud of not botching my Spanish with him! All my languages are rusty at present. While the Liberty Ball had over 13,000, I guessed maybe 1,000 were at the Starlight. Attendees either paid $50,000 to attend and hoped to be approved with a big donor package, or were invited. We did a little lobbying for that ending-double-taxation legislation as members of the House and Senate were milling around. Celebs like Mike Tyson, Jillian Michaels, and Vince Vaughn were in the crowd. I taught Solomon my rock concert skills for holding the rail so that we were only feet away from President Trump and the First Lady, Vice President Vance and the Second Lady, and the Trump family for their dance on the stage. When Fox News lost their feed, Solomon and I each took unobstructed video of the entire thing. You can find mine on my , though I had to lower the resolution there to get it to upload. Last, we heard about some fraud going on with the grifter events dotted outside the recognized celebrations. Promises of celebrities who never had any intention of appearing as part of the VIP packages that were sold using their names. High ticket prices for no adequate food or drink. Promises of a possible Trump appearance that was NEVER ever going to happen. Fines for various violations in the middle of the event. Demands for refunds only to find there would be none... Some of the donors to these cons had literally given enough money that if they'd called me or Solomon, we could have had them at least at unsanctioned balls where they really would have had a genuine inaugural experience. But on the polar opposite of that, we closed our trip with a conversation with the family of an incoming cabinet secretary who reminded us that there are people who really are trying to do right by us, will uphold Trump's agenda, and honestly - are just people who deserve a little grace. We're back home in Oregon now. And it's time to bring this energy shift here ... All I can say is this: ~, baby! | | Oregon Conservative Caucus Update | Help us flip Oregon red! Since my article detailing Donald Trump's "[Muslim Ban 2.0](https://substack.com/redirect/8ca365fa-1a6c-4f3d-894c-3056fbf0636d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" (and hundreds of other fascist Executive Orders) I have received an onslaught of painful messages claiming "_American Muslims are getting what we deserved_." The claim goes that because American Muslims were critical of Biden and Harris for arming Netanyahu, even as he committed war crimes and genocide, they are why Harris lost. Therefore, American Muslims are allegedly to blame for Trump's election, and deserve the cruelty Trump is meting out. The facts and receipts demonstrate that this conclusion is not only racist and cruel, it is flat out false. If we have any hope of stopping Trump's fascism, it is critical we work together, not fight one another. **Let 's Address This.**
**Let's Address This with Qasim Rashid is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..t-mH0A_cDljNauKwFyKvKnaznpIiqAj8iQsNIetvTes?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=151452176)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fde4e15b-6164-40e5-a6d5-89298cd86b68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Pictured: Ishraq Ali [Photo Credit: GETTY]
**I break this short article into three parts:**
1. A snapshot of the cruel, racist, and propagandized comments I've received in response to my article about Trump's Muslim ban 2.0.
2. A clearly laid out factual rebuttal to the disinformation dividing us right now.
3. A call for unity against hate and disinformation

## 1\. A Snapshot of the Racism and Propaganda
People had opinions in response to my article on Trump's Muslim Ban version 2.0. Some were just calloused, concluding they don't care and now Muslims will "find out" the consequences of their actions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/df80a010-e5b2-41e9-9311-e5e79bb3203a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Other responses were much more sinister, making a mockery of the suffering of millions, and further laughing at the idea of American Muslims being "dragged off to one of Trump's gulags." And for good measure, added the same "FAFO" comment.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cd4b982b-e23d-4511-8bdc-851c2d4800cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And yet others delved into the most bizarre disinformation imaginable. While Michigan _actually_ has about 241,000 total American Muslims, somehow that number is now 3.7 million(!) (which would be about 40% of Michigan's total population) who voted for Trump. That would assume that some Muslims also voted for Harris, thus putting the actual number of Muslims in Michigan as easily more than half the state's population.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4c7c2ead-76b4-4e2b-9e95-262857b3c2d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The irony of the above person blaming me for "not doing research," is not lost on me. And it is not just me receiving such hate--I've spoken to dozens of my fellow American Muslims who are on the receiving end of similar backlash. So, while I could share more such grotesque comments and emails, suffice it to say, this disinformation and hate solves nothing. It does accomplish one thing, however--it advances the Trump agenda of fear, disunity, and distrust among American citizens. The more divided we are, the stronger he is. That is why we must rely on facts, truth, and compassion to stand united against hate.
So to set the record straight, what are the facts about American Muslims and the 2024 election?
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..t-mH0A_cDljNauKwFyKvKnaznpIiqAj8iQsNIetvTes?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=151452176)
## 2\. The Facts About American Muslims in the 2024 Election
#### Fact: American Muslims overwhelmingly voted Democrat
Let's start with how American Muslims voted overall and nationwide. According to an [exit poll survey of more than 100,000 voters](https://substack.com/redirect/92b2562f-662d-4563-962d-195aee7cddc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), run in a joint project by the AP and Fox, American Muslims overwhelmingly voted for the Democratic ticket both in 2020 and in 2024. In fact, they voted for Harris by a larger margin (+30%)than they voted for Biden (+29%).
**• 2020: 64% Biden, 35% Trump**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dfd102d4-92d8-414d-8d0b-4930aeb4085c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**• 2024: 62% Harris, 32% Trump**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f208c098-e0d0-42e1-9c4e-5ec2a9a38adc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Moreover, the Harris/Walz ticket didn't just lose Michigan--they sadly lost all seven swing states needed to win the election, including states with an infinitesimal population of American Muslims, and also lost the popular vote. I state this not to pour salt on a wound, but to reiterate that to lay this blame at the feet of an already marginalized and tiny community is simply unfair and illogical. But moreover, we all saw this coming.
#### Fact: Polling Told Us This Could Happen - The Democratic Party Didn't Listen
As [I wrote in my post election analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/d5de84f4-882e-44af-9c12-931460d827cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) documenting what went wrong in the Democratic Party:
> American Muslims comprise of roughly 1% of the United States population. The vote some American Muslims withheld due to Biden's policy on Israel did not impact the election results. But the Biden administration's refusal to listen to 77% of Democrats, 63% of moderates, and 61% of all Americans [who wanted Biden to stop arming Netanyahu], absolutely did.
Yes, months and months before the election, polling confirmed that the Democratic Party would dramatically increase its likelihood of winning in November if it broke from Netanyahu and stopped arming him to commit war crimes and genocide. And, conversely, increase its likelihood of losing if it did not divest from arming Netanyahu.
To reshare what I detailed in Summer 2024, a [YouGov/IMEU Policy Project poll](https://substack.com/redirect/1468fcd1-303a-4878-a22f-d02da9a69a2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) among Democrats and Independents in the swing states of Arizona, Georgia, and Pennsylvania, found that the Harris/Walz path to victory included announcing a cessation of arms to Netanyahu (as our Leahy Laws required).
* In Arizona, 35% of voters said they would be _more_ likely to vote for the Harris if she vowed to stop weapons to Israel. Only 5% said they are less likely to vote for that policy--a 7:1 ratio of voter support in a state Biden won by only 11,000 votes.
* In Georgia, 39% of voters said they are more likely to vote for Harris if she vowed to stop weapons to Israel. Only 5% said they are less likely to vote for that policy--an 8:1 ratio of voter support in a state that Biden won by 12,000 votes.
* In Pennsylvania, 34% of voters in Pennsylvania said they are more likely to vote for Harris if she vowed to stop weapons to Israel. Only 7% said they would be less likely to vote for that policy--a 5:1 ratio of voter support in a state Biden won by only 82,000 votes.

Instead, as well documented, despite Biden's own State Department repeatedly confirming that Netanyahu committed war crimes, Biden continued to arm him. Why is anyone surprised this upset tens of millions of voters (not just American Muslims)? Unsurprisingly, post election [polling](https://substack.com/redirect/eb090931-3af6-49a2-9893-fa028d59e157?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) further affirms that of those who chose not to vote for Harris, the top reason that motivated them to stay home was the Biden administration's decision to continue to fund Netanyahu despite his documented war crimes and genocide, and Harris not distancing herself from him on the issue:
> A [January] poll released by IMEU Policy Project and conducted by YouGov found what few in the Democratic Party have been willing to admit: Vice President Harris lost votes because of the Biden administration's support for Israel's genocide of Palestinians in Gaza. [Overall], 29% of voters nationally who voted for Biden in 2020 and cast a ballot for someone besides Kamala Harris in 2024 say "ending Israel's violence in Gaza" was the top issue affecting their vote choice, with the economy a close second at 24%.
None of this is to argue that Trump will be "better" for Palestinians. He will be a fascist. Likewise, none of this is to play "Monday morning quarterback." It is to establish that the polling repeatedly predicted this loss is what would happen. It is not a surprise. Human rights advocates like myself and many others warned well in advance that this was the risk the Democratic Party ran in continuing to bend the knee to Netanyahu. I, for one, cannot understand why Biden looked at these facts and decided to risk American democracy at the doorstep of Netanyahu's war crimes. Indeed, when our elected officials support grotesque policies--everyone loses.
#### Fact: This Anti-Muslim Demonization is Grounded in Racism and Disinformation
American Muslims have just as much right to petition our government for a redress of grievances as does anyone else--as our Constitution guarantees. For the American Muslim community, and indeed for tens of millions more Americans, the genocide in Gaza was a major issue. It is their Constitutional right to express their outrage. Yet, despite the Democratic Party not listening to the plea of American Muslims, the American Muslim community overwhelmingly voted Blue, outdone only by the Jewish community and by those who ascribe to no faith. This shows that despite the outrage and injustice, American Muslims did realize that Trump is not our savior by any stretch, and were nuanced enough to vote accordingly for Harris.
Meanwhile, American Christians (who still represent the majority of Americans) overwhelmingly voted for Trump three elections in a row. The majority of white Americans (who still represent the majority of Americans) overwhelmingly voted for Trump three elections in a row. To instead direct outrage at an already marginalized community that still overwhelmingly voted for Democrats--despite a genocide impacting their lives and families--is the height of absurdity and absolutely grounded in racism and _otherizing_ of American Muslims. This is not a path for unity, but a path to further enabling Trump. We must demand and do better.

## 3\. A Concluding Call For Unity Against Hate
If you were previously misinformed about the role American Muslims played in the 2024 election, I hope this article helped you rectify your understanding. And I thank you for taking the time to read and understand.
The bottom line is this. We face an existential threat to our Republic in the White House. A man who is clear about his intentions to become a dictator, and is already acting upon that intention. We do not have the time to engage in such demonization--particularly as it is built on disinformation and propaganda. My ask of all my fellow Americans is to recognize that we only survive this administration if we stand united on the principles of justice, while leading with compassion, and holding fast to truth.
That is my commitment to you, and that is why I am grateful for your trust and support. We cannot waste time demonizing one another when the end goal we have is the same--form a more perfect Union built on economic, social, and climate justice, human rights, compassion, separation of religion and state, and with elected officials who believe in democracy, not dictatorship. If that describes you, then I am glad you are here. Thank you for being here.
Let us stand firmly together to make that vision a reality.

After Hurricane Helene devastated North Carolina, Trump and his allies spread false claims that FEMA’s response was biased against Republicans and that funding was being diverted to help undocumented immigrants. clean_body: Californians recovering from wildfires are Trump’s latest target. | As wildfires continue to tear through Southern California, displacing thousands of families and consuming entire neighborhoods, Donald Trump just made one thing clear: He doesn’t care. In a recent Fox News interview, Trump threatened to withhold FEMA disaster relief funds from California. He claimed states should “take care of their own problems.” This is no surprise. Trump has spent years politicizing disaster relief. After Hurricane Helene devastated North Carolina, Trump and his allies spread false claims that FEMA’s response was biased against Republicans and that funding was being diverted to help undocumented immigrants. It wasn’t true — but it didn’t stop him from trying to use the catastrophe to divide the American public and cast doubt on government programs designed to help communities. = As the climate crisis escalates around the country — with more destructive wildfires, hurricanes, and flooding — Trump is pulling the rug out from under communities who need help the most. His priority is to punish his political opponents instead of offering support to those in crisis. It’s appalling. It’s dangerous. And it’s exactly why we can’t afford to sit on the sidelines. No matter how many federal programs Trump guts, no matter how many executive orders he signs, our mission does not change. We are building a firewall of climate leaders to fight back. One leader at a time. One state at a time. We’re electing climate champions who will reject Trump’s destructive agenda, protect communities under attack, and pass bold policies to fight the climate crisis at every level. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Let’s rise to meet this moment, together. subject: Money isn’t speech

body:
Let’s make our government work for everyday people — not the highest bidder.
#
Fifteen years ago this week, SCOTUS handed dark money, corporations, and billionaires the _same_ right to political speech as firefighters, teachers, electricians, and every other working American.
**The result? A political system that is fundamentally broken.**
Citizens United opened the floodgates for unchecked political spending, giving unelected billionaires the power to buy elections, gain unprecedented access, and use that influence to get even richer while the rest of us pay the price.
**But here’s the thing: corporations _aren’t_ people, and money _isn’t_ speech.**
[**It’s time to end Citizens United and make our government work for everyday people — not the highest bidder. If you agree, add your name now.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/signup/em-end-citizens-united/?source=em20250124-1715&akid=1715%2E21716%2E2BwtyR)

Since day one, Pramila has refused corporate PAC money. She was one of the first candidates for Congress to do so.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20250124-4699-footer&t=1&akid=4699%2E420207%2E8Cs5el)
Peter, 15 years ago this week, the Supreme Court’s disastrous decision in _Citizens United v. FEC_ put a price tag on our democracy.
**Since day one, Pramila has refused corporate PAC money. She was one of the first candidates for Congress to do so.** Instead she’s relied on grassroots supporters like you to fuel her campaign.
[**Will you pitch in $3 or anything you can today to help her keep up the fight?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20250124?refcode=em20250124-4699&amount=3&refcode2=4699_420207_8Cs5el&akid=4699%2E420207%2E8Cs5el)

We can see the consequences of _Citizens United_ in last year’s election. Elon Musk poured **$277 million** into the effort to elect Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans in Congress.
_**And that’s only 0.05% of his net worth!**_ For the median American, that’s like spending $128 of your hard-earned savings — except that’s not nearly enough to make Republicans bow at your feet.
There is no reason the ultra-rich should have more influence over our government than everyday families, but that’s exactly what this court decision allows.
**It’s time to end _Citizens United_ and get Big Money out of politics once and for all.**
[**Pramila will keep fighting until we make it happen, but she’s counting on your support to keep going. Please, if you can, pitch in $3 or any amount right now to help us take back our government for working people.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20250124?refcode=em20250124-4699&amount=3&refcode2=4699_420207_8Cs5el&akid=4699%2E420207%2E8Cs5el)

Team Jayapal

President Donald Trump is set to sign the Laken Riley Act, the first bill of his new administration.

The bill is named after Laken Riley, a Georgia nursing student who was killed in 2024, whose name became a rallying cry during Trump’s White House campaign.

If signed into law, the bill would require the detention of unauthorized immigrants accused of theft and violent crimes, according to the Associated Press.

We often talk about history repeating itself, but rarely have we seen it as clearly as we do now. In the 1970s, America’s economy was in disaster mode, plagued by historic levels of inflation and stagnant growth.

Our flawed foreign policy led to the Iranian revolution and the abduction of 66 American citizens in Tehran, which only increased costs at home – costs that had already soared through the roof during a long-term energy crisis.

Since January 2021, over the course of former President Biden’s tumultuous time in the White House, the American people have suffered from very similar conditions to those in the late 1970s. The rate of inflation in 2022 hit a 40-year high, and everyday goods and services, like margarine (56.8% increase), car insurance (47.3% increase), and eggs (40.1% increase), cost significantly more than they did in 2020.

Republican Alabama Sen. Katie Britt will reintroduce legislation Thursday to secure the southern border.

The bill, known as the WALL Act, would appropriate $25 billion to complete the construction of a border wall at the southern border, fulfilling a long-time goal of President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers. Britt’s legislation would be paid for in part by eliminating taxpayer-funded entitlements for illegal migrants and does not increase the national debt, according to background on the bill exclusively obtained by the Daily Caller News Foundation.

“President Donald Trump and the Republican majorities in the House and Senate have not just a mandate but an obligation to secure the border and protect American families,” Britt told the DCNF in a statement. “The United States needs a completed border wall — it is just commonsense to have a physical barrier in place to ensure only lawful entry into our country.”

With less than one week in office, President Trump has made major strides. But what about the impact to a Blue State like Connecticut that is not just blue on the license plate?

[Pledge your support](https://substack..5vglhtAlu2OL60B10o6daf1lXV_ynWKZf6VPo-ZVDGo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=155630635)

I entered the race to challenge Jim Himes on several issues: Healthcare, I-95 and to a plethora of Promises Made/ Promises Broken. Today we will focus on 2 of them I-95 and Broken Promises - Especially in Bridgeport.

We campaigned hard and we made an impact despite a loss. So does the adage to the victor goes the spoils ring true? In this election, the answer is NO as We The People of Connecticut benefited from a challenger like me. Connecticut is getting some help on the federal level due to the pressure (which I am sure will be denied by Jim and the rest of the Democrat representation in Washington).

Let's start with 95.

We put out messages all the time every time I was stuck on the way to one of the 17 towns in my district. We were frustrated that a 30 mile trip would take anywhere from 1-2 hours and then 35 minutes on the way home. My son wrote a song about it and some of the lines "95 will move, our schools will improve...vote Mike, you have to vote for Mike....tell Himes to take a hike."

You might remember this video
[](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1cd4661c-f948-4c16-a336-a6d0804cedb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Right before the election, suddenly work began on I-95 and not that divider nonsense. Yonkers Contracting began work on the exit ramps from Greenwich to Stamford to fix the On and Off Ramps so that one of the 3 lanes would go back to being a lane in use rather than turning a 3 lane highway (on each side) into 2. This literally happened a week from the election. Coincidence I think Not. **Putting Pressure on Our Elected Officials is critical to making progress.**
90% of this $76 million for the I-95 project was being funded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Deal. The plans were drawn up in 2019 as part of a reconstruction project but they magically broke ground just before the election.
**Promise Made/ Promises Broken**
One major focus of our campaign was Bridgeport. One Issue, the Congress Street Bridge.
You might have seen this short reel
[](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ba38db5b-f2b4-48eb-9dfa-a636f50b6a41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It was a promise Jim Himes made in 2008 on his campaign to fix. We went to that bridge, we talked to residents and 16 years later - No Bridge. Well magically, this year, 17 years later, the Bridge was finally approved and funded. Who was at this historic event? Jim Himes, Senator Richard Blumenthal, Senator Chris Murphy (and Mayor Joe Ganim.
So I say, we must continue to be active and put pressure and we will get results. It just may take a little longer in Connecticut. Do not give up. I am not!

Friends,

By now, you have probably heard about Donald Trump’s unforgivable act of treachery—one of his first acts as President after being sworn in was to grant unconditional pardons to January 6 Capitol riot offenders, including defendants who have been prosecuted but haven’t yet had their cases heard before a jury.

Axios reported that Donald Trump’s stated rationale for granting a sweeping pardon for the felons, traitors, white supremacists, and violent criminals who attacked cops and erected a gallows to hang the sitting Vice President from was simply: “ _F-k it._ ”****

# [Thank Bishop Budde for confronting Trump and calling for "mercy" for those who are scared](https://default.salsalabs.org/T1dd4d4bb-017c-4d65-9320-7029a6489a4c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

---
| | | Mariann Edgar Budde, the Episcopal bishop of Washington, delivered a sermon at a service attended by Donald Trump at the National Cathedral -- and made him visibly uncomfortable simply by **[calling on him](https://default.salsalabs.org/T7aacf06e-db61-425a-a615-ced3fca750bb/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** to "show mercy" to the many people in America who are "scared" right now. **In other words -- to act like Jesus would.** Trump went ballistic on social media, and his supporters (including many pretend Christians) **[went on the attack](https://default.salsalabs.org/T028a048d-927f-4f0b-a29e-bd77ab9e02a6/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**. [**We stand proudly with Bishop Budde, thank her for doing the right thing, and for having the guts to stand up to Trump and his followers. Add your name and thank her.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T3e0ec383-ae50-4ef6-bbf8-9c581a01c7af/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)
